findings.title: RDS without IAM database authentication
findings.description: With iam_database_authentication_enabled absent or false, database access relies on long-lived passwords instead of short-lived IAM credentials, weakening credential hygiene.

findings.title: Hardcoded credentials in resource config
findings.description: A database password written as a literal in Terraform config is stored in state, plan output, and version control. The same holds for a secret-like variable or local flowing into a credential attribute. Reference a secrets manager or a generated password instead. The secret value is never included in findings.
findings.expected: reference to a secrets manager or generated password
findings.remediation:
Remove the hardcoded credential and rotate it immediately — it is compromised.
Reference a Secrets Manager secret instead:
data "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "db" {
  secret_id = aws_secretsmanager_secret.db.id
}
# then: password = jsondecode(data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.db.secret_string)["password"]
If the value was committed to git, purge it from history (BFG/truffleHog) and rotate.

findings.title: RDS MySQL/Postgres instance without IAM database authentication
findings.description: MySQL and Postgres RDS instances support IAM database authentication, which replaces long-lived passwords with short-lived IAM credentials. With iam_database_authentication_enabled absent or false, access relies on static passwords. Engine-scoped: only fires for mysql/postgres engines; aurora and unknown engines are out of scope.

findings.title: RDS instance without CloudWatch log exports
findings.description: Hygiene: RDS instances should export database logs to CloudWatch via enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports for auditing and troubleshooting. Without log exports, forensic analysis after an incident is limited.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

findings.title: RDS instance without copy_tags_to_snapshot
findings.description: Hygiene: RDS instances should copy tags to snapshots so backup resources inherit cost-allocation and ownership tags. Set copy_tags_to_snapshot = true.

findings.title: RDS instance without enhanced monitoring
findings.description: Hygiene: RDS instances should enable enhanced monitoring (monitoring_interval > 0) for OS-level metrics that aid troubleshooting. Set monitoring_interval to 1, 5, 10, 15, 30 or 60.
findings.remediation:
Enable Enhanced Monitoring on the RDS instance (1-second OS metrics):
resource "aws_db_instance" "this" {
  # ...
  monitoring_interval = 60
  monitoring_role_arn = aws_iam_role.rds_enhanced_monitoring.arn
}
monitoring_interval accepts 0, 1, 5, 10, 15, 30, or 60 (seconds); any
non-zero value requires a monitoring_role_arn with the
rds-monitoring-role trust policy.

findings.title: RDS Postgres instance without query logging
findings.description: Hygiene: RDS Postgres instances should export postgresql logs to CloudWatch for query auditing. Add "postgresql" to enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

findings.title: RDS instance without Performance Insights
findings.description: Hygiene: RDS instances should enable Performance Insights for query-level performance analysis. Set performance_insights_enabled = true.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: RDS instance on the default option group
findings.description: option_group_name is absent or a default group, so the instance runs with AWS's generic options (e.g. no OEM, no MariaDB audit plugin). Use a purpose-built option group.
findings.evidence: option_group_name = absent (provider default: default option group)
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: RDS master password not managed by Secrets Manager
findings.description: A plaintext master password is set without manage_master_user_password, so the credential sits in state and is never rotated automatically. Use manage_master_user_password = true so RDS manages rotation in Secrets Manager. The password value is never included in findings.
findings.remediation: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them via data sources. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.

findings.title: VPC without DNS hostnames
findings.description: An aws_vpc with enable_dns_hostnames = false (the provider default) gives instances no public DNS hostnames, which breaks hostname-based service discovery and forces reliance on raw IPs. Enable DNS hostnames alongside DNS support.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Key Vault without firewall
findings.description: A Key Vault with no network_acls block, or with network_acls.default_action = "Allow", accepts connections from any network. Restrict access with default_action = "Deny".
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account without blob versioning
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account blob_properties without versioning_enabled loses protection against accidental overwrite or deletion. Enable versioning.
findings.remediation: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time restore / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

findings.title: Storage account without blob soft delete
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account blob_properties without delete_retention_policy cannot recover accidentally deleted blobs. Enable soft delete.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account allows shared key access
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account with shared_access_key_enabled = true permits storage account key authentication. Prefer Microsoft Entra ID and disable shared key access.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account without infrastructure encryption
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account without infrastructure_encryption_enabled lacks double encryption at the infrastructure layer. Enable it for defense in depth.
findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. For storage accounts set `infrastructure_encryption_enabled = true` and use a customer-managed key via `azurerm_key_vault_key`. For regulated data use a customer-managed key in Key Vault with purge protection and key rotation.

findings.title: Storage account without customer-managed key
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account without customer_managed_key block uses Microsoft-managed keys. Use a customer-managed key in Key Vault for sensitive data.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account queue without logging
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account queue_properties without logging loses audit trail for queue operations. Enable queue logging.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on Azure Monitor diagnostic settings, the Activity Log, and Defender for Cloud. Ship logs to a Log Analytics workspace in a security subscription.

findings.title: Key Vault not using RBAC authorization
findings.description: azurerm_key_vault with enable_rbac_authorization = false uses legacy access policies. Prefer Azure RBAC for centralized access control.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Key Vault not using premium SKU
findings.description: azurerm_key_vault with sku_name = "standard" lacks HSM-backed keys. Use premium SKU for hardware-protected keys.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account without private endpoint
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account with no azurerm_private_endpoint targeting it is reachable over the public endpoint. Connect it via a private endpoint on the storage subresource (blob, dfs, queue, table, or file).
findings.evidence: private_endpoint = no azurerm_private_endpoint targets this account
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account without SAS expiry policy
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account without a sas_policy block issues shared access signatures with no enforced expiry. Set sas_policy { expiration_period and expiration_action } to bound SAS lifetimes.

findings.title: Storage account allows cross-tenant replication
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account without allow_cross_tenant_replication = false permits object replication to storage accounts in other Microsoft Entra tenants, enabling data exfiltration paths. Disable cross-tenant replication.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account without blob change feed
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account blob_properties without change_feed_enabled = true records no ordered log of blob create/update/delete events, blinding incident response to data tampering. Enable the blob change feed.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account with public network access (default)
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account without public_network_access_enabled = false exposes the storage endpoint to the internet by default. Disable public network access and use private endpoints instead. (Strict complement of AEGIS-AZURE-006, which covers an explicit true value.)
findings.remediation: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, disable public network access (`public_network_access_enabled = false`), and use private endpoints / Private Link if external access is required. Verify with `az network nsg rule list`.

findings.title: Storage account without network rules
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account without a network_rules block accepts storage traffic from any network by default. Add network_rules with default_action = "Deny" and explicit allow rules. (Strict complement of AEGIS-AZURE-021, which covers an explicit Allow default action.)
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account without managed identity
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account without an identity block cannot use customer-managed keys stored in Key Vault. Enable a system-assigned identity when CMK encryption is required.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Key Vault network ACLs allow public traffic
findings.description: azurerm_key_vault without a network_acls block (default allow) or with default_action other than "Deny" accepts secret/key operations from any network. Set default_action = "Deny" with explicit allowances.
findings.remediation: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, disable public network access (`public_network_access_enabled = false`), and use private endpoints / Private Link if external access is required. Verify with `az network nsg rule list`.

findings.title: Storage account with shared key access enabled
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account with shared_access_key_enabled (the provider default) permits Shared Key authorization, which bypasses Entra ID and cannot be scoped. Disable it and use Entra ID with default_to_oauth_authentication.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account not defaulting to OAuth authentication
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account without default_to_oauth_authentication = true lets clients fall back to Shared Key auth. Default to Entra ID OAuth for data-plane operations.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Azure security best practices and the CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Storage account allows nested public items
findings.description: azurerm_storage_account with allow_nested_items_to_be_public (the provider default) lets containers and blobs be marked public even when account-level public access is off. Disable it to enforce private-by-default.
findings.remediation: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, disable public network access (`public_network_access_enabled = false`), and use private endpoints / Private Link if external access is required. Verify with `az network nsg rule list`.
